items.m03s3q4: Overall, the number of visitors to the Science Museum increased a lot over the period, while the Art Gallery and the History Museum both decreased. The Science Museum became the most popular museum after 2014.
items.m03s3q5: Overall, coal fell a lot while wind and solar increased very much and gas became the biggest source in 2020. Nuclear and hydro didn't change much.
items.m03ckq8: Overall, the youngest group spent the most time on social media and gaming, but older people spent more time on streaming video. Streaming was similar for all ages, while gaming was the least popular for people over 50.
items.m04s3q5: The Science Museum reached nearly 760 thousand visitors in 2020, almost double the number in 2010.
items.m04s3q6: Teenagers spent much more time on social media than people over fifty, about three times more.
items.m04ckq8: Coal dropped from 48% of electricity in 2000 to only 18% in 2020.
items.m06s3q7: The Science Museum started with 420 thousand visitors in 2010 and this number rose every year. In 2014 it reached 570 thousand and passed the Art Gallery, which had 560 thousand. After that the Science Museum continued to grow and finished at 760 thousand in 2020. This was much higher than the History Museum, which only had 260 thousand visitors.
items.m07s3q7: German teachers earned the highest salary. They got 62000 dollars at the start and 81000 after 15 years. Thai teachers earned the lowest salary. This is a very big difference. They got only 9000 dollars at the start and 17000 later, so Germany was about seven times more. Japanese and Korean teachers earned 31000 and 33000 dollars respectively.
items.m08s3q7: Overall, recycling glass is a cycle with eight stages. It begins when used bottles are collected at a bottle bank and it ends when the new bottles are delivered to the shops, and then the cycle starts again.
items.m09s3q7: Overall, the town centre changed from an industrial area to a residential and shopping area. The old factory became apartments and the main road was closed to traffic. The river, the park and the bus station stayed the same.
items.m10s3q7: Finland drank the most coffee, 21 cups per person per week. Thailand drank the least, only 5 cups. Italy and Brazil drank 14 and 12 cups, more than Japan with 8 cups.

plan.big: Science Museum go up, Art Gallery and History Museum go down

slots.what: the number of visitors to three museums in a city in Europe
slots.groupB: the Art Gallery and the History Museum
slots.feature: the Science Museum was the most popular in 2020

p-line-museums.text:
The line graph shows the number of visitors (in thousands) to three museums in a city in Europe from 2010 to 2020.

Overall, the Science Museum had more and more visitors, but the Art Gallery and the History Museum had less visitors. In 2020 the Science Museum was the most popular with 760 thousand visitors.

In 2010, the Science Museum had 420 thousand visitors. It increased to 570 thousand in 2014 and 710 thousand in 2018. In 2020, it was 760 thousand, the highest number. This was almost two times more than 2010.

The Art Gallery had 610 thousand visitors in 2010, more than the Science Museum. But it went down to 560 thousand in 2014 and 520 thousand in 2020. The History Museum was the lowest. It decreased from 380 thousand in 2010 to 260 thousand in 2020. In 2018 it went up a little to 300 thousand.

p-line-museums.short:
The line graph shows the number of visitors to three museums in a European city between 2010 and 2020.

Overall, the Science Museum went up but the Art Gallery and the History Museum went down.

The Science Museum had 420 thousand visitors in 2010 and 760 thousand in 2020. In 2014 it was 570 thousand. It was the highest in 2020.

The Art Gallery had 610 thousand in 2010 and 520 thousand in 2020. The History Museum had 380 thousand in 2010 and 260 thousand in 2020. It was the lowest.

plan.big: young people use social media and gaming a lot, old people less, streaming is the same

slots.what: the hours per week that people in four age groups spent on three activities in 2023
slots.contrast: young people spent the most time on social media and gaming, but old people spent less
slots.exception: streaming video, which was 15 hours for 18–29

p-bar-screentime.text:
The bar chart shows the average number of hours per week that people in four age groups spent on three activities in 2023.

Overall, young people spent the most time on social media and gaming, but old people spent less time. Streaming video was about the same for all age groups, around 12 to 15 hours.

People aged 13–17 spent 21 hours a week on social media, and people aged 18–29 spent 18 hours. The 30–49 group spent 11 hours and the 50+ group spent only 6 hours. Gaming was 12 hours for the 13–17 group, 8 hours for 18–29, 3 hours for 30–49 and 1 hour for 50+.

Streaming video was different. The 18–29 group watched the most, 15 hours. The 13–17 group watched 14 hours, the 50+ group watched 13 hours and the 30–49 group watched 12 hours.

Streaming video was different. The 18–29 group watched the most, 15 hours. The 13–17 group watched 14 hours, the 50+ group watched 13 hours and the 30–49 group watched 12 hours.

plan.big: eight steps, old bottles to new bottles, it is a cycle

slots.product: how glass bottles are recycled in eight steps
slots.start: old bottles in the bottle bank
slots.st1: people put the old bottles in the bottle bank and a lorry transports them to the recycling plant
slots.st2: the bottles are washed with high-pressure water
slots.st3: workers sort the bottles by colour and the glass is crushed into small pieces, called cullet
slots.st4: is melted in the furnace at 600–800 °C
slots.st5: the hot glass is moulded into new bottles
slots.st6: the new bottles are filled and delivered to the shops

p-proc-glass.text:
The diagram shows how glass bottles are recycled in eight steps.

Overall, there are eight stages in this process. It starts with old bottles in the bottle bank and it finishes when new bottles go to the shops. Then it starts again.

First, people put the old bottles in the bottle bank. Second, a lorry transports the bottles to the recycling plant. Third, the bottles are washed with high-pressure water. Fourth, workers sort the bottles by colour, clear, green and brown. Fifth, the glass is crushed into small pieces, called cullet.

Sixth, the cullet is melted in the furnace at 600–800 °C, and they add new raw material. Seventh, the hot glass is moulded into new bottles. Finally, the new bottles are filled and delivered to the shops. I think this is a good process for the environment.
p-proc-glass.revised:
The diagram shows how glass bottles are recycled in eight steps.

Overall, there are eight stages in this process. It starts with old bottles in the bottle bank and it finishes when new bottles go to the shops. Then it starts again.

First, people put the old bottles in the bottle bank. Second, a lorry transports the bottles to the recycling plant. Third, the bottles are washed with high-pressure water. Fourth, workers sort the bottles by colour, clear, green and brown. Fifth, the glass is crushed into small pieces, called cullet.

Sixth, the cullet is melted in the furnace at 600–800 °C, and they add new raw material. Seventh, the hot glass is moulded into new bottles. Finally, the new bottles are filled and delivered to the shops. I think this is a good process for the environment.

plan.big: the town changed a lot, more buildings and a hospital, temple and river the same

slots.place: the centre of a small town in north-eastern Thailand
slots.change: changed a lot and had more new buildings
slots.extended: the main road became wider with four lanes

p-map-thai-town.text:
The maps show the centre of a small town in north-eastern Thailand in 2005 and in 2025.

Overall, the town changed a lot. There were more new buildings in 2025 and a new hospital, but the temple and the river were the same.

In 2005, there was a wet market, an open field and a temple in the north of the main road. In 2025, the wet market became a covered market and the open field became a car park. The temple did not change. The main road became wider with four lanes.

In the south, there were wooden houses and rice fields in 2005. In 2025, the wooden houses became townhouses, and a hospital was built on the rice fields. The rice fields were smaller. Also, the ferry on the river changed to a bridge.

plan.big: smartphone go up to 95% and basic phone go down to 5%

slots.what: the percentage of teenagers who had a smartphone and who had a basic mobile phone
slots.feature: in 2025 almost all teenagers had a smartphone

p-line-phones.text:
The line graph shows the percentage of teenagers in one country who had a smartphone and who had a basic mobile phone from 2010 to 2025.

Overall, more and more teenagers had a smartphone, but fewer teenagers had a basic phone. In 2025, 95% had a smartphone and only 5% had a basic phone.

In 2010, only 10% of teenagers had a smartphone. It went up to 30% in 2013, 60% in 2016, 80% in 2019 and 90% in 2022. In 2025 it was 95%.

Basic phones were the opposite. In 2010, 80% of teenagers had a basic phone. It went down to 65% in 2013 and 40% in 2016. Then it was 20% in 2019, 10% in 2022 and 5% in 2025. The two lines crossed between 2013 and 2016.
